name: hra-integration
title: HRA API Integration — Datasets, Ontology, and BioModel Digital Objects
lead:
This investigation builds the HRA (Human Reference Atlas) side of the
fetch-and-compare spine, following an explicit arc: name-match -> annotation-
match -> shown in the Atlas Browser. It starts with a thin CCF-API client +
Steps (Task A) and a biomodel-DO annotation layer using name-synonym
matching over the HRA reference-organ set (Task B) — recall-limited because
it only scans the model title (glucose-biomodel-do: 5/25, 20%; full corpus:
82/1,096, 7.5%). It then adds a second, higher-recall matcher that reads
each model's own curated SBML MIRIAM/BTO annotations instead of its title
(annotation-organ-matching: 114/1,096, 10.4%, 14 organs, driven almost
entirely by BTO->organ crosswalk hits), and measures exactly how much
coverage that adds over name-only matching (annotation-recall-gain: +85
models, +4 organs, union 167/1,096 across 14 organs). The payoff of both
matchers existing is not the index alone: it's that the resulting
organ->models catalogs are what feeds the HRA Computational Model Atlas
(`studies/hra-atlas-browser/viz/atlas/`), the actual interactive 3D view
where a biomodel's organ tag becomes something a user can click on. This
realizes the DynXR proposal's Aim 2 T2.1 (HRA dataset access) and T1.1/T2.4
(transparent organ gap-filling for biomodel annotation, now with a visible
endpoint in the Atlas Browser); see references/sources/dynxr-proposal.md.
question:
Can we pull HRA datasets/knowledge via the live CCF API (reference organs,
cell-type terms, anatomical-structure terms) and link BioModels to HRA
anatomy (Uberon organs) via a transparent biomodel Digital Object +
organ->models index — and, having built that index, actually get the
resulting models onto the HRA atlas as something a user can see?
hypothesis:
The HRA CCF API's reference-organs, cell-type-term-occurences, and
ontology-term-occurences endpoints are stable enough to drive a Step-based
fetch inside a process-bigraph composite; and simple synonym matching over
BioModels names against the HRA reference-organ set is enough to annotate a
useful fraction of glucose-regulation models with an Uberon organ, giving a
working organ->models index without a heavyweight NLP classifier.
Confirmed: live runs loaded 81 reference organs (69/81 Uberon-keyed),
149 Cell Ontology terms, and 288 anatomical-structure terms; synonym
matching over 25 "glucose regulation" search hits tagged 5/25 (20%) with
an HRA organ — 4 pancreas, 1 liver — a real but recall-limited (name-only)
organ->models index, not a complete one.

acceptance_criteria.behavior: The HRA CCF reference-organs endpoint returns a non-empty, Uberon-annotated organ list with per-sex GLB assets.
The HRA CCF cell-type-term-occurences endpoint returns a non-empty, count-sorted Cell Ontology term list.
The HRA CCF ontology-term-occurences endpoint returns a non-empty, count-sorted anatomical-structure term list.
At least one glucose-regulation BioModel is tagged with at least one HRA organ, and the organ->models index is inspectable (not a black box).

The committed annotation catalog (datasets/biomodel_annotation_catalog.json) tags at least 100 corpus models with an HRA organ, and every organ tag traces to a specific CVTerm (curie, qualifier, element) via the BTO->organ crosswalk or a direct Uberon/FMA match — not a black box.

annotation_gain.compare_catalogs over the committed name-synonym and annotation catalogs shows annotation-based matching adding at least 50 models and at least 2 whole organs over name-only matching, with a union organ->models index inspectable per-organ (not just an aggregate delta).

The committed corpus DB (datasets/model_hra_map.json) harvests all 1,096 curated BioModels, each with molecular ids + publication link + HRA organ/FTU/cell-type mapping, loads network-free via BiomodelHraMapStep (cache-or-load), and reports measured corpus coverage (89% molecular, 20% Uberon, 10% HRApop) — with the DB downloadable as a registered workspace dataset.

executive.what_is_this:
Builds the HRA (Human Reference Atlas) side of the fetch-and-compare
spine, then closes the loop into the Atlas Browser: a thin CCF-API
client (reference organs, cell-type terms, anatomical-structure terms);
a biomodel Digital Object annotation layer with two complementary organ
matchers — name-synonym matching over BioModels titles, and
annotation-based matching over each model's own SBML MIRIAM/BTO
metadata; a measured comparison of how much recall the annotation
matcher adds over name-only matching; and the HRA Computational Model Atlas
(`studies/hra-atlas-browser/viz/atlas/`) that renders the resulting
organ->models index as an interactive 3D atlas a user can actually see
biomodels attached to.
executive.verdict:
All three HRA CCF endpoints load real, non-empty, correctly-shaped
data (81 reference organs 69/81 Uberon-keyed, 149 CL terms, 288
anatomical-structure terms). Name-synonym matching tags 82/1,096
models (7.5%) across 10 organs — biologically correct where it fires,
but recall-limited because it only scans the model title. Annotation-
based matching (SBML MIRIAM + BTO crosswalk) tags 114/1,096 (10.4%)
across 14 organs, adding 85 models and 4 whole organs (lymph-node,
ovary, spleen, urinary-bladder) the name matcher cannot reach at all;
the union of both reaches 167/1,096 models (15.2%) across 14 organs.
The two matchers are complementary, not redundant — pancreas is the one
organ where name-only matching (36) beats annotation matching (24)
individually, though the union (47) still exceeds either — and that
combined organ->models catalog is what the Atlas Browser renders.

decisions_needed.question: Resolved: SBML MIRIAM/BTO annotation matching (annotation-organ-matching, annotation-recall-gain) raised full-corpus recall from 82/1,096 (7.5%) to a 167/1,096 (15.2%) union across 14 organs. Should the union (not name-only) become the default organ->models index the Atlas Browser and downstream coverage studies key off?
decisions_needed.context: annotation-recall-gain's fp-union-organ-index followup proposes re-running model-coverage-3d/corpus-coverage against the union index; the Atlas Browser currently renders whatever organ->models index is passed to it, so this is a live wiring decision, not just an analysis one.

decisions_needed.question: How much more organ coverage would extending the 32-entry BTO->organ crosswalk unlock?
decisions_needed.context: 278 corpus models carry a BTO term at all, but only 114 resolve to an organ through the current crosswalk (annotation-organ-matching's fp-bto-crosswalk-extension followup) — 985/1,096 models (89.9%) remain untagged by either matcher combined.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
A thin Step-based client against the live HRA CCF API is stable enough
to drive a process-bigraph composite; name-synonym matching over
BioModels titles builds a real but recall-limited organ->models index;
reading each model's own SBML MIRIAM/BTO annotations instead of its
title materially raises that recall without a heavyweight NLP
classifier; and the resulting organ->models catalog is what feeds the
HRA Computational Model Atlas, turning "which organ is this biomodel tagged to" into
something a user can see and click on in an interactive 3D atlas.
evidence_for: hra-reference-organs: 81 organs load, 69/81 (85.2%) Uberon-keyed, 45 female / 36 male entries.
hra-cell-types: 149 distinct CL terms load, count-sorted, top term at 2,762 occurrences.
hra-anatomical-structures: 288 distinct terms load, top term matching hra-cell-types' top count exactly (cross-endpoint consistency check).
glucose-biomodel-do: organ_to_models correctly concentrates on pancreas (4 models) and liver (1 model) — exactly the two organs glucose-homeostasis biology predicts.

annotation-organ-matching: annotation-based matching tags 114/1,096 models (10.4%) across 14 organs, 92.9% of the underlying CVTerm hits (156/168) resolving via the curated BTO->organ crosswalk rather than a direct Uberon/FMA MIRIAM match — the organ signal in BioModels curation practice is dominated by BTO, not Uberon/FMA.

annotation-recall-gain: annotation matching adds 85 models and 4 whole organs (lymph-node, ovary, spleen, urinary-bladder) that name-only matching (82 models/10 organs, 7.5%) never reaches, for a union of 167 models/14 organs (15.2% of the 1,096-model corpus) — a strict recall improvement across almost every organ, the one exception being pancreas (name 36 > annotation 24, though the union of 47 still exceeds either alone).
caveats: Name-synonym matching is 7.5% of the full corpus (82/1,096) and annotation matching only reaches 10.4% (114/1,096) — even their union (167/1,096, 15.2%) leaves 89.9% of the corpus untagged by either matcher.
14.8% of reference organs (12/81) parse to a non-Uberon FMA identifier and are silently dropped by downstream Uberon-only matching.

The 32-entry BTO->organ crosswalk is curated, not exhaustive: 278 corpus models carry a BTO term at all, but only 114 resolve to an organ through it — extending the crosswalk is the most direct lever to raise recall further.
Annotation matching does not strictly dominate name matching per-organ: pancreas is name-favored (36 vs 24), so the union, not either matcher alone, is the recommended organ->models index.

studies.name: annotation-organ-matching
studies.title: Annotation-Based Organ Matching — SBML MIRIAM + BTO Crosswalk Provenance
studies.question:
How does a BioModels entry get tagged with an HRA Uberon organ when the
match comes from its embedded SBML MIRIAM annotations rather than its
name — and which biological CVTerm qualifiers / ontologies actually carry
that organ signal?

resolved_uncertainties: BTO-mediated matching (via the curated crosswalk), not direct Uberon/FMA MIRIAM annotation, is the dominant organ-tagging mechanism in this BioModels corpus (156 vs 12 hits).
remaining_uncertainties: How much more organ coverage would extending the 32-entry BTO->organ crosswalk unlock, given 278 corpus models carry a BTO term at all vs the 114 that currently resolve to an organ?

followup_study_proposals.title: BTO->organ crosswalk extension
followup_study_proposals.motivation: 278 models carry a BTO term but only 114 resolve to an organ through the current 32-entry crosswalk; extending the crosswalk against the remaining BTO terms in the corpus could raise annotation-based organ-tagging recall further.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Enumerate the distinct BTO terms present across all 278 BTO-annotated corpus models, identify which are absent from the current 32-entry crosswalk, and curate organ mappings for the highest-frequency gaps.

findings.statement:
Of the 168 CVTerm hits behind the annotation catalog's 114 organ-tagged
models, 156 (92.9%) resolve through the curated BTO->organ crosswalk
and only 12 (7.1%) through a direct Uberon/FMA MIRIAM match --
BTO-via-crosswalk is the dominant, not incidental, organ-matching
mechanism, and `BQB_OCCURS_IN`/`BQB_IS` are the dominant qualifiers
(88 and 40 of 168 hits).

evidence.summary: ontology_counts: BTO 156, UBERON 12; qualifier_counts: BQB_OCCURS_IN 88, BQB_IS 40, BQB_IS_VERSION_OF 35, BQB_IS_PART_OF 4, BQB_HAS_PART 1; 114/1,096 models tagged (10.4%), 14 organs.

biological_validation.basis: The qualifier/ontology breakdown matches expected BioModels curation practice: tissue/cell-line context (BTO) is annotated far more often than direct anatomical ontology terms (Uberon/FMA), and 'occurs in'/'is' qualifiers dominate over compositional part-of relationships.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline annotation-organ-matching composite (committed catalog scan) completed without error.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 makes the annotation-matching mechanism transparent and falsifiable: the BTO->organ crosswalk, not direct Uberon/FMA annotation, is what does 92.9% of the work, directly motivating crosswalk-extension as the next lever (see annotation-recall-gain).

derived.insight:
Of the 168 CVTerm hits behind the annotation catalog's 114 organ-tagged
models, 156 (92.9%) resolve through the curated BTO->organ crosswalk
and only 12 (7.1%) through a direct Uberon/FMA MIRIAM match --
BTO-via-crosswalk is the dominant, not incidental, organ-matching
mechanism, and `BQB_OCCURS_IN`/`BQB_IS` are the dominant qualifiers
(88 and 40 of 168 hits).

studies.name: annotation-recall-gain
studies.title: Annotation Recall Gain — Annotation-Matching vs Name-Only Organ Tagging
studies.question:
How much organ/model coverage does annotation-based organ matching (SBML
MIRIAM + BTO crosswalk) add over the existing name-synonym matcher
(`glucose-biomodel-do`/`corpus-coverage`), across the full 1,096-model
curated BioModels corpus?

resolved_uncertainties: SBML MIRIAM/BTO annotation-based matching materially raises organ-tagging recall over name-only synonym matching (+85 models, +4 organs), directly answering glucose-biomodel-do's followup proposal fp-sbml-annotation-tagging.
remaining_uncertainties: Would a combined name+annotation matcher (the union index) change conclusions in downstream studies that currently key off the name-only organ_to_models index (model-coverage-3d, corpus-coverage)?

followup_study_proposals.title: Union organ->models index for downstream coverage studies
followup_study_proposals.motivation: model-coverage-3d and corpus-coverage currently key off the name-only organ_to_models index; re-running them against the union (name + annotation) index would widen their AS-node/organ-GLB coverage numbers using the same crosswalk machinery.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Re-run CoverageStep with a catalog built from the union of the name-synonym and annotation catalogs' organ_to_models indices, and compare AS-node/organ-GLB coverage against the current corpus-coverage baseline (635/1,730 AS nodes, 31/114 organs).

findings.statement:
Annotation-based organ matching reaches 114/1,096 models (10.4%,
14 organs) vs name-only matching's 82/1,096 (7.5%, 10 organs) over
the same 1,096-model corpus, adding 85 models and 4 whole organs
(lymph-node, ovary, spleen, urinary-bladder) the name matcher cannot
reach because those organ names never appear verbatim in a BioModels
title -- confirming annotation-based matching is a materially
higher-recall complement to, not merely a duplicate of, name-synonym
matching.

evidence.summary: name: 82 models/10 organs (7.5%); annotation: 114 models/14 organs (10.4%); union: 167 models/14 organs; delta: +85 models, organs_added=[lymph-node, ovary-female-left, spleen, urinary-bladder].

biological_validation.basis: The 4 newly-reached organs (lymph-node, ovary, spleen, urinary-bladder) are biologically plausible SBML-annotation-only gains -- organs rarely named in a model title but directly encoded in curated MIRIAM/BTO metadata -- and annotation matching adds models name-matching misses for nearly every name-matched organ, with pancreas the one organ where name-matching alone tags more, consistent with annotation matching reading richer per-model metadata than a title string.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline recall-gain composite (compare_catalogs over both committed catalogs) completed without error.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 quantifies, for the first time, exactly how much of the name-only matcher's recall ceiling (glucose-biomodel-do's central open question) SBML-annotation-based matching closes: +85 models, +4 organs, union coverage of 167/1,096 (15.2%) vs either matcher alone.

derived.insight:
Annotation-based organ matching reaches 114/1,096 models (10.4%,
14 organs) vs name-only matching's 82/1,096 (7.5%, 10 organs) over
the same 1,096-model corpus, adding 85 models and 4 whole organs
(lymph-node, ovary, spleen, urinary-bladder) the name matcher cannot
reach because those organ names never appear verbatim in a BioModels
title -- confirming annotation-based matching is a materially
higher-recall complement to, not merely a duplicate of, name-synonym
matching.
